title_vi: Tartuffe, hay Kẻ giả đạo đức
translation_direction: fr → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete French electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Molière’s brisk comic verse is rendered as speakable Vietnamese lines, one per French line, with rhyme only where it comes naturally; Dorine’s pertness, Pernelle’s scolding and Tartuffe’s unction keep their registers, and the Préface and Placets are elegant periodic prose.
decisions.rationale: Forced rhyme added filler and blurred sense in a test round and was dropped.

decisions.decision: The French text comes from French Wikisource’s Louandre edition; the editor’s Notice, footnotes and verse numbers were removed.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Mme Pernelle’s ‘j’en rabats de moitié’ (I esteem it half as much) was garbled as ‘I will visit half as often’; corrected.
‘Grands élancements’ was rendered unintelligibly and made Elmire a target of Tartuffe’s reproaches; now ‘những cơn xúc động dâng cao’.
Orgon called Tartuffe ‘hắn’ (contempt that belongs to Dorine); now ‘ông ấy’.
Dorine’s ‘son frère’ (Mariane’s brother Damis) was ambiguous; now named.
Tartuffe’s ‘je ne suis rien moins que ce qu’on pense’ (I am anything but what people think) was blurred; corrected by hand after a review.
In the Orgon–Tartuffe scene the address pair drifted to ‘anh’ for every ‘vous’; now Tartuffe says ‘ông’ and Orgon ‘ngài’, with ‘anh’ only for ‘mon frère’.
Cléante’s ‘il’ (Damis, the rightful heir) read as Orgon or Tartuffe; now ‘cậu ấy’ (fixed by hand).
Elmire’s single rhetorical question was split into stacked ‘nếu’ clauses with no main clause; rewritten as one question.
‘Taisez-vous. C’est le mot qu’il vous faut toujours dire’ was inverted (it is the word to be said to Dorine); corrected.
Cléante’s argument had lost the antecedent of ‘il’ (ce zèle); restored.

The Exempt’s ‘sa conduite’ (Tartuffe’s lead) was mistranslated, and ‘la retraite d’un ami’ (a friend’s flight) was read as Orgon sheltering him; both corrected, the second by hand after the last review.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: Couvrez ce sein que je ne saurais voir.
glossary.draft_rendering: Che cái ngực ấy đi, tôi không chịu nổi khi nhìn thấy.
glossary.rationale: The famous line, kept in one wording.

glossary.draft_rendering: ông ấy (Orgon, Pernelle, Mariane) / hắn (Dorine, Damis, Elmire) / ông ta (Cléante)
glossary.rationale: The pronoun is a character’s verdict on Tartuffe.

glossary.draft_rendering: Tartuffe: tôi/ông; Orgon: tôi/ngài; ‘mon frère’ → anh
glossary.rationale: Reverence of the dupe, unction of the deceiver.

witness_decision: Selected the French Wikisource transcription of Tartuffe ou l’Imposteur from Charles Louandre’s edition (Œuvres complètes de Molière, Charpentier, 1910, vol. II, texts validated); the project did not collate it with the 1669 first edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Long speeches by Cléante keep only occasional rhyme; the lines are speakable but plainer than the verse.
The Loyal/déloyal pun is rendered in plain sense (‘chẳng trung thực chút nào’).
A stiff intensifier ‘mới’ in Tartuffe’s lines.

title_review.target_title: Tartuffe, hay Kẻ giả đạo đức
title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Tartuffe, hay Kẻ giả đạo đức’ (Tartuffe, or the Hypocrite); no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening of the Préface: the play’s long persecution.
